title: Character sets
starter: A vending machine has 4 buttons. How many different combinations of two presses are there? What about 8 buttons?
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: Text as numbers
facts: Every character has a number, called its character code.
The code is stored in binary, like any other number.
The computer uses a character set to know which code means which character.
stations.challenge: Convert the first letter of your name into binary.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Every character has a number, called its character code.
Also credit: The code is stored in binary, like any other number.

questions.q: The letter A has the character code 65. Show 65 in 8-bit binary.

questions.a: A collection of characters and the binary codes used to represent them

stations.name: ASCII
facts: ASCII uses 7 bits, giving 128 different characters.
It covers English letters, digits, punctuation and control codes.
Extended ASCII uses 8 bits for 256 characters.
stations.challenge: How many characters can 7 bits represent, and why?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: ASCII uses 7 bits, giving 128 different characters.
Also credit: It covers English letters, digits, punctuation and control codes.

questions.q: How many characters can 7-bit ASCII represent?
Why was ASCII not enough for the whole world?
questions.a: It has no room for other alphabets, such as Arabic, Chinese or Greek

stations.name: The ASCII pattern
facts: Codes are in order: A is 65, B is 66, and so on.
Lower case starts 32 later: a is 97.
The digits 0 to 9 are codes 48 to 57.
stations.challenge: If A is 65, what is E? And what is e?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Codes are in order: A is 65, B is 66, and so on.
Also credit: Lower case starts 32 later: a is 97.

questions.q: If A is 65, what is D?
Why is the gap between A and a exactly 32?
questions.a: It makes converting between upper and lower case easy: just add or subtract 32

stations.name: Unicode
facts: Unicode was designed to represent every writing system in the world.
It uses 16 bits or more, giving tens of thousands of characters.
It includes emoji, and the first 128 codes match ASCII.
stations.challenge: Give two advantages and one disadvantage of Unicode compared with ASCII.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Unicode was designed to represent every writing system in the world.
Also credit: It uses 16 bits or more, giving tens of thousands of characters.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of Unicode over ASCII?
questions.a: It can represent characters from every writing system, not just English

questions.q: What is the main disadvantage of Unicode?
questions.a: It uses more bits per character, so files are larger

stations.name: Bits and characters
facts: The number of bits decides how many characters can be represented: 2 to the power n.
2 bits give 4; 4 bits give 16; 8 bits give 256.
Add one bit and you double the number of characters.
stations.challenge: How many binary combinations are there with 2, 4 and 8 bits?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: The number of bits decides how many characters can be represented: 2 to the power n.
Also credit: 2 bits give 4; 4 bits give 16; 8 bits give 256.

questions.q: How many different characters can 4 bits represent?
A character set has 1,000 characters. How many bits are needed per character?

stations.name: Text file size
facts: File size = number of characters × bits per character.
The same message in Unicode is roughly twice the size of 8-bit ASCII.
Spaces and punctuation count as characters.
stations.challenge: Calculate the size of a 1,000-character message in ASCII and in 16-bit Unicode.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: File size = number of characters × bits per character.
Also credit: The same message in Unicode is roughly twice the size of 8-bit ASCII.

questions.q: A message has 250 characters stored in 8-bit ASCII. How big is it in bytes?
The same message is stored in 16-bit Unicode. How big is it now?

final.name: Final challenge: spell it in binary

questions.q: The letter H has the character code 72. Show 72 in 8-bit binary.
This binary is a character code: what is it in denary? (It is the letter i.)
Does each statement describe ASCII or Unicode?
questions.a: Uses 7 bits for 128 characters = ASCII; Represents every writing system in the world = Unicode; Uses 16 bits or more per character = Unicode; Enough for English letters, digits and punctuation = ASCII; Includes emoji = Unicode; Produces smaller text files = ASCII

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

exam.q: State what is meant by a character set.
points: Every character has a number, called its character code.
The computer uses a character set to know which code means which character.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark for a correct answer.

exam.q: Explain why Unicode uses more storage than ASCII.
points: The same message in Unicode is roughly twice the size of 8-bit ASCII.
ASCII uses 7 bits, giving 128 different characters.
Extended ASCII uses 8 bits for 256 characters.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 2.

exam.q: A character set uses 8 bits per character. State how many characters it can represent.
points: File size = number of characters × bits per character.
Every character has a number, called its character code.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark for a correct answer.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
